Sample Name: Routine Followup - Hypertension and Laboratory Review
Description: General medicine follow-up for blood pressure, potassium abnormalities, smoking, and occupational exposure concerns.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient feels generally well without new cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, abdominal pain, or weight loss. He requests a screening chest x-ray because of tobacco use, work as a chemist around potentially carcinogenic chemicals, and historical Agent Orange exposure. The physicians explain that prior pulmonary CT imaging was less than one year earlier, and no immediate repeat chest imaging is indicated in the discussion. He continues smoking and is ambivalent about cessation. He has a history of diverticulitis without current abdominal symptoms and a longstanding facial skin discoloration which he attributes to earlier exposure. There is also concern about an ill relative with metastatic cancer, discussed without implying that the patient has cancer. Potassium remains mildly low despite supplementation, and urinalysis showed mild proteinuria with preserved renal function.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Blood pressure satisfactory. General, lung, abdominal, and oral examinations were performed without an acute abnormality documented in the encounter.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Hypertension with mild proteinuria. Increase lisinopril from one-half tablet to one tablet daily, monitor home blood pressure, and return to the prior dose if hypotension or intolerance occurs.
2. Mild hypokalemia. Continue monitoring and dietary counseling regarding potassium-containing foods. The lisinopril increase may also influence potassium.
3. Tobacco use and prior occupational exposures. Discussed smoking cessation and existing lung imaging; repeat imaging deferred at this visit.
4. Weight management and preventive care. MOVE program discussed. Seasonal influenza vaccination and prior pneumococcal vaccination reviewed.
5. Return in three months.
